record.paper_title: Recent results and open questions on collective type phenomena from A-A to pp collisions
record.original_question: What experimental and theoretical mechanism explains the multiplicity-dependent collective-type trends observed in proton-proton collisions at √s = 7 TeV, including the decrease of kinetic freeze-out temperature, the increase of average transverse expansion velocity, and identified-hadron transverse-momentum spectral changes that resemble trends seen in heavy-ion collisions?

evidence.quote: One could conclude that for pp collisions at 7 TeV , the Tkin - < βT > correlation as a function of charged particle multiplicity has a trend rather similar with the one observed in heavy ion collisions, i.e. the freeze-out kinetic temperature decreases and the average transverse expansion velocity increases with charged particle multiplicity (pp) or increasing centrality (A-A).

Although these preliminary results seem to indicate that for events with high charged particle multiplicity in pp collisions at 7 TeV collective type phenomena show up, the experimental and theoretical efforts to understand the physics behind the evidenced trends remain to be done.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In high-energy proton–proton collisions at center-of-mass energy √s = 7 TeV, transverse-momentum spectra of identified hadrons (π, K, p, …) measured in classes of increasing charged-particle multiplicity, when fitted with blast-wave-type (hydrodynamically inspired) parametrizations, exhibit the following trends as multiplicity grows: (i) the extracted kinetic freeze-out temperature T_kin decreases; (ii) the average transverse expansion (radial flow) velocity ⟨β_T⟩ increases; (iii) the identified-hadron p_T spectra harden in a mass-ordered way. These trends qualitatively mirror the centrality dependence observed in heavy-ion (A–A) collisions, where they are attributed to the formation of a thermalized, collectively expanding partonic medium (quark–gluon plasma).

Problem: Identify and characterize the underlying physical mechanism — experimentally testable and theoretically formulated — that produces these multiplicity-dependent collective-type signatures in pp collisions at √s = 7 TeV. Specifically:
(a) Provide a dynamical model (e.g., hydrodynamic evolution of a small thermalized droplet, color reconnection between multi-parton interactions, string/color-rope formation, parton percolation, initial-state color-glass-condensate correlations, or hadronic rescattering) that quantitatively reproduces the joint evolution of (T_kin, ⟨β_T⟩) and the identified-hadron p_T spectra as functions of charged-particle multiplicity.
(b) Determine whether the observed collectivity in high-multiplicity pp events arises from genuine final-state collective expansion of a thermalized system, from initial-state momentum correlations, or from non-collective hadronization mechanisms, and propose experimental observables that discriminate among these scenarios.
artifact.category_tag: High-energy heavy-ion and pp collision phenomenology
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2019–2025) confirms that collective-type signatures in high-multiplicity pp collisions at 7 TeV — decreasing T_kin, increasing ⟨β_T⟩, mass-ordered spectral hardening, long-range ridge, strangeness enhancement — are now well established experimentally, but the underlying mechanism remains debated. Candidate explanations include hydrodynamic flow in a small QGP droplet, color reconnection among multi-parton interactions, string/color-rope and percolation models, initial-state CGC correlations, and hadronic rescattering. No single mechanism has been shown to reproduce all observables, so the problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: Multiplicity dependence freeze-out scenarios in pp collisions at √s = 7 TeV
status_evidence.snippet: Growing transverse flow velocity and decreasing non-extensivity parameter with multiplicity may be understandable in terms of more active collective dynamics in high-multiplicity pp.
status_evidence.claim: The mechanism is interpreted via increasing collectivity but is not uniquely established.

status_evidence.title: Event-shape and multiplicity dependence of freeze-out radii in pp at 7 TeV
status_evidence.snippet: Trends in pp resemble those in A–A but may also be due to color reconnection, MPI, percolation, or hadronic rescattering, not exclusively QGP.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple non-equivalent mechanisms remain viable, indicating an open question.

status_evidence.title: Thermal freeze-out and collective signatures in pp collisions (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent non-extensive statistical study of energy/pseudorapidity systematics of freeze-out parameters in pp collisions, still investigating origin of collective trends.
status_evidence.claim: Investigation of the mechanism continues into 2025.
